title: Let's Go Karaoke!
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Satomi Oka, a boy soprano leading his middle-school choir in its final competition, is approached by yakuza member Kyouji Narita, who needs singing lessons: his boss holds karaoke contests where the worst singer gets a tattoo applied painfully by the boss himself (Yen Press blurb via AniList and MangaUpdates; Anime UK News review). Over the lessons an unlikely bond grows while Satomi worries his voice is about to break (review). Yama Wayama's one-volume comedy, first self-published at COMITIA and later adapted to anime and live action.
life_message: It suggests that an honest, unexpected friendship can help a young person through the change of growing up.

content.note: Threat of a painful punishment tattoo (blurb); MangaUpdates Violent Character/s; no violent scenes described (review).
Hint that Satomi may be in danger (review).

AniList tags Boys' Love and Age Gap, but MangaUpdates lists BL Subtext and Non-BL with Two Male Leads, and the review describes a non-romantic bond between an adult and a middle schooler. No sexual content noted.
Adolescent anxiety over a changing voice (review).
A middle schooler meets an adult gang member alone for lessons (blurb); played for comedy.

dominant: Coming of age, unlikely friendship, voice and identity changing
